verdicts.why: The classical-element sense names one of the four elements of an old cosmology; it is a technical label with no attitude toward its referent.
A legal agreement with a penalty clause is named in plain legal terms; the word takes no side on the agreement or the parties to it.
A written promise to repay a debt is a financial instrument named neutrally; debt is an unpleasant referent, not a loaded word.
Putting something forward for consideration is a plain act; the verb carries no approval or scorn for the thing proposed or the proposer.
Nominating someone for an office or honour is described without judgement; the verb neither praises nor belittles the nominee.
In the sense of a youthful male person the word simply names age and sex; the dismissive use of boy for a grown man belongs to a different sense, and the gloss is binding.
As a male human offspring, the plain counterpart of girl and son, the word states a kinship fact and carries no attitude beyond it.
